newsitem.title: FRANCE: French aerospace industry body optimistic for 1997.
newsitem.headline: French aerospace industry body optimistic for 1997.

text.p: A pick-up in the French aerospace industry observed in 1996 should continue in 1997, Serge Dassault, chairman of the GIFAS industry association, said on Tuesday.

Unconsolidated 1996 turnover for the French aerospace industry rose 7.2 percent to 108.4 billion francs, thanks to a recovery in civil orders and military exports, he said at the annual briefing of the Groupement des Industries Francaises Aeronautiques et Spatiales.
"We estimate turnover for 1997 of 116 billion francs, or a seven percent increase compared to 1996," he said.

"In the context of a dollar close to its economic exchange rate and the recovery in civilian orders, we are on the whole optimistic," he said. A recovery in military orders, through the defence budget law and multi-year orders, was needed to confirm the expansion in the industry, he added.
New orders in 1996 exceeded turnover, rising 13.5 percent to 118.4 billion francs.
Exports, which accounted for 65 percent of the total with 58.1 billion francs, increased by 27.9 percent. Military exports, up 26.2 percent, rose as well as civil, up 28.4 percent.
The industry cut some 1,500 jobs last year to 96,000 and expects the total to stabilise in 1997.
Dassault also said that in spite of the promising numbers, significant cuts in French military orders as well as heavy social payroll contributions weighed on the sector last year.
Dassault is also chairman of Dassault Aviation.
